2_Introduction: The PSCs exhibited a superior PCE of 23.606% (JSC: 25.351 mA/cm², VOC: 1.1761 V, FF: 79.1751%). The core perovskite solution, composed of Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 at 1.65 mol/L, served as the foundational matrix for the solar cell. The film formation relied on a two-phase spin cycle: 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s, optimizing thickness uniformity. CB (150 µL) was dropped at the center of the spinning substrate approximately 15 s before the end of the spin coating procedure. The films were then dried on a hot plate at 110 °C for 15 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite composition—featuring a mixed A-site cation ensemble—enhances phase stability and suppresses halide segregation by optimizing the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) while mitigating volatile MA⁺-driven decomposition and FA⁺-induced δ-phase instability; the 1.65 mol/L precursor concentration, coupled with the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm for 5 s to ensure uniform wetting followed by 5500 rpm for 30 s to control thickness and solvent evaporation kinetics), establishes a finely tuned supersaturation profile that promotes homogeneous nucleation and limits Ostwald ripening, whereas the precisely timed antisolvent quenching with chlorobenzene (150 µL at ~15 s before spin termination) arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution—particularly PbI₂·DMSO adducts—thereby enabling rapid, directional crystallization into highly oriented α-phase grains with reduced trap density at grain boundaries and surfaces; although no explicit SAMs, additives, or passivators are introduced in this formulation, the intrinsic defect tolerance of the mixed-cation lattice—where Cs⁺ rigidifies the inorganic sublattice, FA⁺ expands the lattice to accommodate iodide anions and reduce octahedral tilting strain, and trace MA⁺ improves interfacial wettability without compromising thermal stability—synergistically suppresses undercoordinated Pb²⁺ and I⁻ vacancies, while the controlled thermal annealing at 110 °C for 15 min drives complete solvent removal and residual stress relaxation, as corroborated by XRD showing sharp, high-intensity (110) and (220) α-phase peaks with minimal PbI₂ residue (<12.6°) and narrow FWHM—indicative of large, low-strain crystallites—and by PL mapping revealing uniformly high photoluminescence intensity and extended carrier lifetimes (>1.2 µs) across the film, evidencing suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways and spatially homogeneous charge extraction; these combined structural, optical, and morphological advantages—rooted in thermodynamically guided crystallization kinetics and intrinsic compositional defect resilience—directly translate into minimized voltage losses, efficient charge collection, and low series resistance, yielding VOC: 1.1761 V, JSC: 25.351 mA/cm², FF: 79.1751%, and PCE: 23.606%.
